phases.title: Build skeleton
phases.goal: a Norm-clean `coders/` that builds `codexion` with the deliverable Makefile (cc -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pthread, NAME/all/clean/fclean/re, no relink), a `main.h` with the base types and a minimal `main.c`

phases.title: Argument parsing and validation
phases.goal: parse and validate the 8 arguments into a config with reusable primitives (one shared trim of surrounding whitespace for numbers, digits only, overflow-safe up to INT_MAX, per-field minimums, scheduler exactly fifo/edf); any invalid input prints a specific error and the usage to stderr and exits non-zero before allocating or starting threads

phases.title: Time and serialized logging
phases.goal: millisecond clock relative to the simulation start (gettimeofday), a stop-aware sliced sleep, and a mutex-serialized logger that prints the five subject state lines and nothing after the stop except the burnout line

phases.title: Priority queue
phases.goal: a hand-written binary min-heap of dongle requests ordered by key then arrival ticket, supporting the fifo key (arrival ticket) and the edf key (last_compile_start + time_to_burnout)

phases.title: Simulation state init and teardown
phases.goal: build the `t_sim` (coders, dongles with mutex/cond/heap, stop and log mutexes, seat-to-dongle mapping with 1 dongle for 1 coder) and tear it down completely, cleaning up partial initialisation on any malloc or pthread init failure without leaks

phases.title: Dongle arbitration
phases.goal: atomic two-dongle acquisition (a coder takes both only when it is the head of both dongle heaps and both are available with cooldown elapsed, mutexes locked lower-index first), release with cooldown, pthread_cond_timedwait waits with no busy-wait and wake-all on stop, with arbiter-level tests (head-of-both rule, fifo/edf ordering, cooldown, stop wake-up) as evidence for the PLAN.md progress argument

phases.title: Coder thread
phases.goal: the coder routine loops take dongles, compiling, release, debugging, refactoring with correct logs, updates last_compile_start and compile_count under its own mutex, and exits promptly on stop (single coder takes its only dongle and waits to burn out)

phases.title: Monitor thread
phases.goal: a separate monitor thread that detects a burnout and logs it within 10 ms, or detects that every coder reached number_of_compiles_required, then sets stop and wakes all waiting threads

phases.title: Simulation lifecycle
phases.goal: main wires parse, init, start the coder and monitor threads, join and teardown end to end, with clean shutdown on pthread_create failure and the edge cases (1 coder, zero compiles required) behaving as specified

phases.title: Hardening and README
phases.goal: prove the whole program against the subject with full-binary simulation tests (fifo/edf ordering, cooldown, no burnout under edf at and above the PLAN.md viability boundary including the N = 6 interleaved case, typical evaluation runs, valgrind leak-free, TSan race-free, Norm-clean) and complete the README with its mandatory sections, real outputs and didactic tone

features.title: Request order
features.goal: the dongle request type and its strict order (key, then arrival ticket), plus the fifo/edf key computation with no overflow

acceptance.criterion: smaller key first: `{key 5, ticket 9}` before `{key 6, ticket 1}` returns 1 and the reverse call returns 0
equal keys, ticket breaks the tie: `{key 7, ticket 2}` before `{key 7, ticket 3}` returns 1 and the reverse returns 0
strict: a request compared with itself, or with a copy that has the same key and ticket, returns 0 (both orders)
`coder` plays no part: two requests with the same key and ticket and different `coder` return 0 both ways, and swapping the `coder` values of AC1/AC2 pairs does not change their results

extreme values, no subtraction overflow: `{LONG_MIN, 0}` before `{LONG_MAX, 0}` returns 1 and the reverse 0; `{0, LONG_MIN}` before `{0, LONG_MAX}` returns 1 and the reverse 0; `{-1, 5}` before `{0, 0}` returns 1

total order on a sample: for every pair of distinct elements `a`, `b` of a fixed sample of at least 8 requests (distinct `(key, ticket)`, mixed signs, ties on key), the results are exactly 0 or 1 and match the lexicographic `(key, ticket)` order (exactly one of `before(a, b)` and `before(b, a)` is 1); for every triple, if `before(a, b) == 1` and `before(b, c) == 1` then `before(a, c) == 1`
NULL: `a == NULL`, `b == NULL` or both return 0 with no crash
the arguments are read only: both requests are byte-for-byte unchanged after every call
`make -C coders` builds `codexion`, the binary defines `is_request_before` (`nm`), and `norminette coders/` reports no error
fifo: `get_request_key(MODE_FIFO, t, s, b)` returns `t` for `t` in `{0, 1, 42, LONG_MAX}`, whatever `s` and `b` are (including `s = -1`, `s = LONG_MAX`, `b = 0`, `b = -1`)

edf: `get_request_key(MODE_EDF, 3, 1000, 410)` returns 1410; `(MODE_EDF, 0, 0, 1)` returns 1; the result does not depend on the ticket (`ticket` 0, 7 and `LONG_MAX` give the same key for the same `s`, `b`)
edf upper bound: `s = LONG_MAX - INT_MAX`, `b = INT_MAX` returns `LONG_MAX`; `s = LONG_MAX - INT_MAX + 1`, `b = INT_MAX` returns -1; `s = LONG_MAX`, `b = 1` returns -1

invalid input returns -1: `ticket` of -1 and `LONG_MIN` (both modes); edf with `s` of -1 or `LONG_MIN`; edf with `b` of 0, -1 or `INT_MIN`; a `mode` value that is neither `MODE_FIFO` nor `MODE_EDF` (e.g. `(t_mode)7`)
every valid result is `>= 0`, so -1 never collides with a key: checked on all the valid calls of AC1-AC3
`make -C coders` builds `codexion`, the binary defines `get_request_key` (`nm`), and `norminette coders/` reports no error

features.title: Heap storage
features.goal: a fixed-capacity request heap whose array is allocated and freed explicitly, with overflow-checked sizing and a safe repeated free

acceptance.criterion: `init_heap(&heap, 2)` on a zeroed `t_heap` returns 0, `heap.items != NULL`, `heap.size == 0`, `heap.capacity == 2`; the test then writes and reads back all 2 `t_request` slots and frees `heap.items` with `free`. Repeated with a non-live `t_heap` prefilled byte-wise with a sentinel pattern: same successful result
capacity 1 and capacity 1000 behave as AC1 (every slot writable, `capacity` equals the argument, `size == 0`)

invalid capacity: 0, -1 and `INT_MIN` return -1 and leave the whole `t_heap` byte-for-byte unchanged (the test fills it with a sentinel pattern first and compares the bytes, without evaluating the sentinel pointer)
`init_heap(NULL, 2)` returns -1 with no crash

two heaps of capacity 2 initialised one after the other and kept alive: every slot is filled with distinct field values, and modifying either array leaves the other's fields unchanged (fields compared, not padding); both arrays are then freed
`make -C coders` builds `codexion`, the binary defines `init_heap` (`nm`), and `norminette coders/` reports no error
after `init_heap(&heap, 4)` returned 0, `free_heap(&heap)` leaves `heap.items == NULL`, `heap.size == 0`, `heap.capacity == 0`

for each `n` in `{0, 2, 4}`: initialise a fresh heap of capacity 4, write `items[i] = (t_request){i, i, i + 1}` for `0 <= i < n`, then set `size = n`; `free_heap` leaves NULL/0/0 (no push/pop operation is required)
idempotent: a second and a third `free_heap` on the same heap are no-ops (no crash, fields stay NULL/0/0)
a zeroed `t_heap` (never initialised) and `free_heap(NULL)` are accepted with no crash; the zeroed heap stays NULL/0/0

reuse: after `free_heap`, `init_heap(&heap, 2)` on the same struct returns 0 with `items != NULL`, `size == 0` and `capacity == 2`; both slots are writable and read back what was written; a final `free_heap` leaves NULL/0/0
`make -C coders` builds `codexion`, the binary defines `free_heap` (`nm`), and `norminette coders/` reports no error

features.title: Heap operations
features.goal: push, peek and pop on the min-heap (sift up/down on the request order); a rejected operation (full, empty) leaves the heap and the output untouched

acceptance.criterion: on an empty heap of capacity 4, pushing `{key 9, ticket 1, coder 2}` returns 0, `size == 1` and `items[0]` equals the pushed request field by field

the head is the minimum: on a heap of capacity 8, after each push of the sequence `(key, ticket)` = `(5,1) (3,2) (8,3) (3,0) (1,4) (9,5) (1,9) (7,6)` (coder = position + 1), every push returns 0, `size` grows by 1 and `items[0]` is the smallest request pushed so far by `is_request_before` (4.1.1): the successive heads are `(5,1) (3,2) (3,2) (3,0) (1,4) (1,4) (1,4) (1,4)`, compared field by field with the corresponding input request

heap property and content: after AC2's 8 pushes, for every `i` in `[1, size)` `is_request_before(&items[i], &items[(i - 1) / 2])` returns 0, and `items[0..size)` is a permutation of the 8 pushed requests (every field compared)

fifo and edf ties: pushing keys all equal to 100 with tickets `4, 2, 3, 1` gives the ticket-1 request at the head; pushing fifo-style requests (`key == ticket`) with tickets `3, 1, 2` gives ticket 1 at the head
full: on a heap of capacity 2 holding 2 requests, a third push returns -1 and the whole `t_heap` struct and both slots are unchanged (fields compared); on capacity 1 the same with 1 request

invalid arguments: `push_request(NULL, &req)`, `push_request(&heap, NULL)` and both NULL return -1 with no crash; for the NULL-request case the oracle uses a non-full heap with live entries and fills every unused slot with sentinel field values before taking the snapshot: after the call all heap fields and every slot `[0, capacity)` are unchanged, compared field by field
by value: after a successful push, changing the caller's `t_request` variable leaves the stored copy unchanged; the pushed argument itself is not modified by the call

extremes and larger sizes: a heap of capacity 64 filled with 64 requests of pseudo-random keys (generator in the test notes, `LONG_MIN` and `LONG_MAX` included, unique tickets): every push returns 0, `size` increases by one, the occupied slots are a permutation of the input prefix, the AC3 heap property holds after every push and the minimum is at the head
`make -C coders` builds `codexion`, the binary defines `push_request` (`nm`), and `norminette coders/` reports no error
after pushing `{key 9, ticket 1, coder 2}` into an empty heap of capacity 4, `get_head_request(&heap, &out)` returns 0 and `out` equals the pushed request field by field

it copies the minimum: after each push of the 4.3.1 AC2 sequence (`(5,1) (3,2) (8,3) (3,0) (1,4) (9,5) (1,9) (7,6)`, coder = position + 1) into a heap of capacity 8, it returns 0 and `out` equals, field by field, the request with the successive heads `(5,1) (3,2) (3,2) (3,0) (1,4) (1,4) (1,4) (1,4)`

read only: before each call the oracle snapshots the heap fields and every slot `[0, capacity)` (unused slots filled with sentinel field values); after the call they are unchanged, field by field; two calls in a row give the same `out`

empty: on a freshly initialised heap, and separately after initialising a capacity-1 heap, successfully pushing `{key 9, ticket 1, coder 2}` and setting `heap.size = 0`, it returns -1; the sentinel-prefilled `out` and the heap remain unchanged, field by field

invalid arguments: `get_head_request(NULL, &out)` returns -1 and leaves `out` unchanged; `get_head_request(&heap, NULL)` on a non-empty heap and both NULL return -1 with no crash, the heap unchanged as in AC3
by value: after a successful call, changing `out` leaves the stored head unchanged (a second call returns the original values)
`make -C coders` builds `codexion`, the binary defines `get_head_request` (`nm`), and `norminette coders/` reports no error
after pushing `{key 9, ticket 1, coder 2}` into an empty heap of capacity 4, `pop_request(&heap, &out)` returns 0, `out` equals the pushed request field by field and `size == 0`

sorted order: after pushing the 4.3.1 AC2 sequence (`(5,1) (3,2) (8,3) (3,0) (1,4) (9,5) (1,9) (7,6)`, coder = position + 1) into a heap of capacity 8, eight pops each return 0, `size` decreases by one each time, and `out` equals, field by field, the input requests in the order `(1,4) (1,9) (3,0) (3,2) (5,1) (7,6) (8,3) (9,5)`; a ninth pop returns -1

heap property after each pop: in AC2 and AC5, after every successful pop, for every `i` in `[1, size)` `is_request_before(&items[i], &items[(i - 1) / 2])` returns 0, and `items[0..size)` is a permutation of the requests still queued (every field compared)
empty: on a freshly initialised heap, and after AC1 emptied a heap, it returns -1; the sentinel-prefilled `out`, the heap fields and every slot `[0, capacity)` are unchanged, field by field

larger sizes and extremes: 64 requests from the 4.3.1 AC8 generator (`LONG_MIN` and `LONG_MAX` included, unique tickets) pushed into a heap of capacity 64, then popped: 64 pops return 0 and give the requests in strictly increasing `(key, ticket)` order (each `out` is `is_request_before` the next), covering every input exactly once

interleaved: on a heap of capacity 4, the fixed script `push(4,1) push(2,2) pop push(3,3) push(1,4) pop pop push(5,5) pop pop` (key, ticket; coder = ticket) returns 0 everywhere and the pops give the tickets `2, 4, 3, 1, 5` in that order; the heap ends empty

dongle-sized heap: capacity 2: push `{7,1,1}`, push `{7,0,2}`, pop, pop all return 0 and the outputs equal the second and first requests respectively, field by field; capacity 1: push/pop `{9,1,1}`, then push/pop `{3,2,2}`, all return 0 and reproduce each request field by field

invalid arguments: `pop_request(NULL, &out)` returns -1 with `out` unchanged; `pop_request(&heap, NULL)` on a non-empty heap returns -1 with the heap fields and every slot `[0, capacity)` unchanged; both NULL return -1 with no crash
`make -C coders` builds `codexion`, the binary defines `pop_request` (`nm`), and `norminette coders/` reports no error

features.title: Seat mapping
features.goal: map each 0-based seat to its two dongle indices, lower index first, with a single shared dongle when there is one coder and no overflow at the int bounds

acceptance.criterion: N = 4: seats 0, 1, 2, 3 return 0 with `(first, second)` = `(0, 1)`, `(1, 2)`, `(2, 3)`, `(0, 3)` (the last seat wraps to dongle 0 and still gets the lower index first)
N = 1: seat 0 returns 0 with `first == second == 0` (one coder, one dongle)
N = 2: seats 0 and 1 both return 0 with `(0, 1)` (both coders share both dongles); for every valid seat of AC1 and AC3, `first < second`

int bounds, N = `INT_MAX`: seat 0 gives `(0, 1)`, seat `INT_MAX - 2` gives `(INT_MAX - 2, INT_MAX - 1)`, seat `INT_MAX - 1` gives `(0, INT_MAX - 1)`, all returning 0 with no overflow (clean under `-fsanitize=undefined` if the oracle uses it)

invalid input returns -1 and leaves both outputs unchanged (the test prefills them with a sentinel, e.g. -42): seat -1, seat `INT_MIN`, seat == N, seat > N (N = 4); N of 0, -1 and `INT_MIN` (seat 0); `first` NULL, `second` NULL (valid seat and N, the non-NULL output still unchanged)

features.title: Dongles
features.goal: initialise one dongle (mutex, cond, capacity-2 request heap, available, never released) and the array of N dongles, rolling back exactly what succeeded on any failure, and tear them down in reverse

acceptance.criterion: on a zeroed `t_dongle`, `init_dongle(&dongle)` returns 0 with `available == 1`, `released_at == -1`, `heap.items != NULL`, `heap.size == 0`, `heap.capacity == 2`. Repeated on a non-live `t_dongle` prefilled byte-wise with a sentinel pattern: same result. The test then tears it down by hand (`free_heap`, `pthread_cond_destroy`, `pthread_mutex_destroy`, each returning 0)
the mutex is initialised and unlocked: `pthread_mutex_trylock` succeeds right after the call and `pthread_mutex_unlock` returns 0

the cond is initialised and paired with the mutex: holding `mutex`, `pthread_cond_timedwait` with an absolute deadline already in the past returns `ETIMEDOUT` (the caller owns the mutex again and unlocks it); `pthread_cond_broadcast` returns 0
the heap holds exactly the two neighbours: two `push_request` calls with distinct requests return 0, a third returns -1, and `get_head_request` returns the one `is_request_before` places first

two dongles initialised one after the other are independent: with the first's mutex locked by the test, a `pthread_mutex_trylock` on the second succeeds; their `heap.items` differ, and a push into one leaves the other's `heap.size` at 0
`init_dongle(NULL)` returns -1 with no crash
after `init_dongle(&dongle)` returned 0, `destroy_dongle(&dongle)` returns 0 and leaves `heap.items == NULL`, `heap.size == 0`, `heap.capacity == 0`

with requests still queued (two `push_request` calls after `init_dongle`, `heap.size == 2`), and after `available` and `released_at` were changed by the test (0 and 1234), it returns 0 and the heap is reset as in AC1
after the mutex was used (locked and unlocked by the test) and the cond was used (one `pthread_cond_broadcast` and one `pthread_cond_timedwait` with a past deadline), it returns 0

reuse: after `destroy_dongle`, `init_dongle` on the same struct returns 0 and the dongle works (`pthread_mutex_trylock` succeeds and is unlocked, two pushes succeed, a third fails); a second `destroy_dongle` returns 0 and resets the heap
`destroy_dongle(NULL)` returns -1 with no crash
the test `malloc`s an array of 3 `t_dongle`, initialises all of them with `init_dongle`, pushes one request into each heap; `free_dongles(array, 3)` returns 0

partial array: an array of 4 prefilled byte-wise with a sentinel pattern, only elements 0 and 1 initialised with `init_dongle`; `free_dongles(array, 2)` returns 0 and never touches elements 2 and 3 (no invalid access, no destroy of an uninitialised mutex/cond: valgrind and TSan clean)
count 0: a `malloc`'d array with no initialised element; `free_dongles(array, 0)` returns 0 and the array is freed (valgrind: no leak)
`free_dongles(NULL, 0)` returns 0 with no crash; `free_dongles(NULL, 3)` returns -1 with no crash
negative count: on an array of 1 initialised dongle, `free_dongles(array, -1)` returns -1 and touches nothing (the test then calls `free_dongles(array, 1)`, which returns 0)

`init_dongles(&dongles, 4)` returns 0 with `dongles != NULL`; every element has `available == 1`, `released_at == -1`, `heap.size == 0`, `heap.capacity == 2`, `heap.items != NULL`, and its mutex is unlocked (`pthread_mutex_trylock` succeeds, then unlocked). The test then calls `free_dongles(dongles, 4)`, which returns 0
`n = 1` and `n = 200` behave as AC1 (every element initialised, then freed with `free_dongles(dongles, n)`)

the elements are independent: with element 0's mutex locked by the test, `pthread_mutex_trylock` on element 1 succeeds; every `heap.items` differs; a push into element 2 leaves element 3's `heap.size` at 0

invalid input returns -1 and leaves the out-pointer unchanged (the test prefills it with a non-NULL sentinel address it never dereferences): `n` of 0, -1 and `INT_MIN`; and `init_dongles(NULL, 4)` returns -1 with no crash

invalid input returns -1 and leaves the out-pointer unchanged (prefilled with a non-NULL sentinel address never dereferenced): `n` of 0, -1 and `INT_MIN`; `sim` NULL (n = 4); and `init_coders(NULL, &sim, 4)` returns -1 with no crash

features.title: Simulation
features.goal: build the whole `t_sim` (config, stop/log/ticket mutexes, dongles, coders) in a fixed order with a full reverse rollback on any failure, and free all of it; threads are not started here (phase 09)

acceptance.criterion: full simulation built by hand by the test (the three mutexes `stop_mutex`, `log_mutex`, `ticket_mutex` initialised, `config.number_of_coders = 3`, `init_dongles(&sim.dongles, 3)` and `init_coders(&sim.coders, &sim, 3)` returned 0): `free_sim(&sim)` returns 0 and leaves `sim.dongles == NULL` and `sim.coders == NULL`
partial arrays: with the three mutexes live and `dongles` built but `coders == NULL`, it returns 0 and leaves both NULL; with the three mutexes live and both arrays NULL, it returns 0

after use (every mutex locked and unlocked once, one push into a dongle heap, a coder's `compile_count` set to 2) and with `stopped = 1`, `start_ms = 1000`, `next_ticket = 7`, it returns 0 and leaves `config`, `start_ms`, `stopped` and `next_ticket` unchanged
reuse: after `free_sim`, the test builds the same simulation again on the same struct (as AC1) and a second `free_sim` returns 0 with both arrays NULL
`n = 1` (one coder, one dongle) behaves as AC1
`free_sim(NULL)` returns -1 with no crash

with the config `4 800 200 200 200 3 50 edf`, `init_sim(&sim, &config)` returns 0; `sim.config` equals the input field by field; `start_ms == 0`, `stopped == 0`, `next_ticket == 0`; the 4 dongles have `available == 1`, `released_at == -1`, `heap.size == 0`, `heap.capacity == 2`; coder `i` has `id == i + 1`, the dongle pair of seat `i`, `last_compile_start == 0`, `compile_count == 0` and `sim == &sim`; `stop_mutex`, `log_mutex`, `ticket_mutex`, every dongle mutex and every coder mutex are unlocked (`pthread_mutex_trylock` succeeds, then unlocked). The test then calls `free_sim(&sim)`, which returns 0
`number_of_coders` 1 (one coder, `first_dongle == second_dongle == 0`, one dongle) and 200 (every coder's two indices in `[0, 200)`, the last one `(0, 199)`) behave as AC1
the phase 03 state functions work on the built simulation: `is_stopped(&sim)` returns 0; after `set_stopped(&sim)`, `is_stopped(&sim)` returns 1
on a `t_sim` prefilled byte-wise with a sentinel pattern (owning nothing live), a valid call gives the same result as AC1

invalid input returns -1 and leaves the whole `t_sim` byte-for-byte unchanged (sentinel-prefilled, compared with `memcmp`): `config` NULL; `number_of_coders` 0 and -1. `init_sim(NULL, &config)` returns -1 with no crash
reuse: `init_sim`, `free_sim`, `init_sim` again on the same struct (with a different `number_of_coders`, 3 then 5), `free_sim`: every call returns 0

issues.title: refactor: replace parse_config bit mask with invalid flags [2.3]
issues.goal: parse_config reports invalid arguments through an int invalid[9] flag array instead of a bit mask, with no change in user-visible behaviour

acceptance.criterion: `parse_config(argv, &config, invalid)` on `{"codexion","4","800","200","200","200","3","50","edf",NULL}` returns 0, sets `invalid[1]` to `invalid[8]` to 0 and fills the eight `t_config` fields with 4, 800, 200, 200, 200, 3, 50 and `MODE_EDF`

with `invalid[1]` to `invalid[8]` pre-filled with a garbage value (42), a call with only positions 2, 3 and 8 invalid returns 3 and leaves exactly `invalid[2]`, `invalid[3]` and `invalid[8]` at 1 and the other five positions at 0, so the caller never has to zero the array
all eight arguments invalid returns 8 with `invalid[1]` to `invalid[8]` all at 1; a sentinel stored in `invalid[0]` before the call is unchanged after it, in this and every other case

a single invalid argument at each position `pos` in 1..8 (numeric values `"-1"`, `"abc"`, `""`, `"2147483648"`; scheduler `"FIFO"`, `" edf"`, `"rr"`), all others valid, returns 1 with only `invalid[pos]` set to 1; every `argv` string is byte-for-byte unchanged after the call

the binary is unchanged for the user: `./codexion 4 -5 abc 200 200 3 50 rr` writes the error lines for positions 2, 3 and 8 in that order, then the usage exactly once, nothing to stdout, exit status 1; a single invalid argument writes its own error line then the usage, status 1; `./codexion 4 800 200 200 200 3 50 edf` exits 0 with empty stderr
`make -C coders` builds `codexion`, `norminette coders/` reports no error, and an invalid run under valgrind reports no leak and no error
